questions.answer: Wave intensity is power transferred by the wave per unit area normal to the direction of energy transfer. Its SI unit is W m⁻².
accepted_alternatives: power per unit area, with the area perpendicular to energy transfer
questions.unit_policy: Unit required for the second mark.

marking_points.text: States that intensity is wave power transferred per unit area normal to the direction of energy transfer.
Gives the SI unit W m⁻².

option_feedback.A: A displacement-time graph follows one chosen position through successive times.
option_feedback.B: Graph height is displacement, not energy transferred by each particle.
option_feedback.C: Correct. A displacement-distance graph is a simultaneous snapshot of particles at different positions.
option_feedback.D: A wave graph is a representation of measured displacement, not a particle's path.

marking_points.text: Selects C: a displacement-distance graph shows displacements at different positions at one instant.

questions.unit_policy: Unit is included in the selected option.

option_feedback.A: This reverses the division and does not use I=P/A.
option_feedback.C: This subtracts area from power, which does not calculate power per unit area.
option_feedback.D: This multiplies power by area instead of dividing.

marking_points.text: Selects B: 4.0 W m⁻².

option_feedback.A: The question fixes the wave power, so it does not have to increase.
option_feedback.B: The power is stated to be the same, not smaller.
option_feedback.C: For fixed power, a larger area gives less power through each unit area.
option_feedback.D: Correct. I=P/A, so increasing A at fixed P decreases I.

marking_points.text: Selects D: intensity decreases because fixed power is spread over a larger area.
Uses rectangular area 0.30 × 0.20.
Obtains 0.060 m².

parts.tolerance: Accept 600 to two or more significant figures.
parts.unit_policy: W m⁻² required for the final mark.

marking_points.text: Uses I=P/A.
Substitutes 36 W and 0.060 m² consistently.
Obtains 600 W m⁻².

parts.answer: A = 4πr² = 4π(4.0)² = 201 m², or 2.0 × 10² m² to two significant figures.

marking_points.text: Uses A=4πr² with r=4.0 m.
Obtains approximately 2.0 × 10² m².
Uses I=P/A with 80 W and the spherical area from part (a).
Obtains 0.40 W m⁻².

parts.answer: A larger spherical surface has a larger area. The same 80 W is therefore distributed over more square metres, so the power per unit area and hence the intensity are smaller.
accepted_alternatives: fixed total power gives lower intensity when spread over greater area

marking_points.text: States that a larger spherical surface has a larger area over which the power is distributed.
Explains that the same power per larger area gives a smaller intensity.

parts.answer: The wave transfers energy. Channel particles oscillate as the pulse passes and return to their equilibrium positions, so there is no net transfer of matter with the pulse.
accepted_alternatives: energy travels but the medium does not travel with it

marking_points.text: States that energy is transferred by the progressive wave.
Explains that particles oscillate and return to equilibrium with no net transfer of matter.
Uses power as energy transferred divided by time.
Obtains 6.0 W.

parts.unit_policy: W m⁻² required for the final mark.
